title: Structure, safety and the unit
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What gives the people you lead a sense of structure and safety?

Jose said that the military gives people a massive structure, thought out for them, and it creates a sense of safety: I know where I am and what I am supposed to be doing. He gave the example of a film in which prisoners released after years found the world without rules unsettling.
He said that, as entrepreneurs, we have to develop that structure for ourselves, or we are toast, and develop it for other people too.

Jose said that he reads military history because it has many cases of units that outperformed others. He asked leaders to write down a framework: why was this unit successful? What is the dashboard for a successful unit?

He said the first factor was cultural identity together with what is called task cohesion: why people bond together to act for the good of the group. Unit cohesion is a military concept in which people sustain their will, have a commitment to each other and are mission oriented.
A student said: the people around you play a huge part in contributing to the environment.
What would make your team feel it belongs to something bigger than a task?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the structure your team has now.
Write what makes it feel safe or not.
Write your team's identity in one line.
Write how people commit to each other.
Write the mission that holds it together.

check.q: What did Jose say structure creates?
What did Jose call why people bond to act for the group?
What did a student say plays a huge part in the environment?

recap: Give structure and safety. Build identity and cohesion.
